newsitem.title: USA: US rate rise likely to be quarter of point - report.
newsitem.headline: US rate rise likely to be quarter of point - report.

text.p: The likely rise in short-term interest rates signaled by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan would be no more than a quarter of a percentage point, the Washington Post reported Friday.

Greenspan, in testimony before the Joint Economic Committee of Congress Thursday, set the stage for an increase in interest rates next week when he stressed the importance of prompt action to keep inflation down before it hurts the U.S. economy.
"Fed officials said any increase would be no more than a quarter of a percentage point," the Washington Post reported.
In his testimony, Greenspan said the economy retains a "great deal of vigor" and called the prospects for a continued upswing "quite favorable."
The Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets Tuesday to consider raising short-term rates for the first time in over two years.

"Should we choose to alter monetary policy, we know from past experience that, although the financial markets may respond immediately, the main effects on inflationary pressures may not be felt until late this year and in 1998," Greenspan said.
